01
Summary · one page

What it is, who it is for, and what already works

iHisobchi is the business operating system of Uzbekistan. Documents and digital signature, deals, money, inventory, HR, tax and sales — in one loop, run by an AI agent that knows this particular business. It is operated by conversation.

The problem we solve

The state moved documents, cash registers, HR and payments into electronic form. Business was never given the tool to play by those rules: it keeps nine disconnected programs and carries the same data between them by hand.

Who it is for

Half a million organisations that the law obliges to do the same work every day. 350 thousand of them are already connected to the state e-document system.

What is built

17 modules, 18 surfaces, 24 types of state document, 67 operations available to the AI agent. The product runs in production with legally valid document flow.

Where the innovation is

An AI that lives inside one country's state infrastructure — it knows the invoice, the classifier code and the tax deadline. It is operated by voice. Not one global platform in this category has walked into its own country's state systems.

17business modules on one core
67operations the AI performs itself
137,617documents the system serves
101,429deals assembled, 75% closed
59,354bank operations parsed
86organisations in the system

What we say honestly, up front

The audience is early. Of the 137,617 documents, 136,879 are a mirror of what businesses were doing in Didox anyway, and only 740 were created inside the product. We pull the whole history in so that deals assemble across past years.

The constraint today is not build speed but turning what is built into regular use. We say this first, because figures without that distinction mislead.

Next: the cost of the problem in money, the product in a minute, real product screens, what clients say, the effect for the country and the team. Then the full breakdown: market, every module, architecture, security, economics and horizons.

What happens between "I need a document" and "the deal is closed"

Real screens · not mock-ups

Three screens that carry the whole idea

The home screen. Signed and pending documents, the amount, counterparties, recent documents — and the voice assistant at the top, one tap away. Business Pulse sits in the right column, ready to run a full check-up.

The AI assistant. Chat or voice, one switch apart. The suggested questions are real operations: "how many deals are open?", "which documents await my signature?", "what is my balance?", "who did I send a contract to and never got a power of attorney back?"

Business Pulse. One number for the health of the company, money in and out for the period, the tax-registration status, and below it the movement of money by day, where it came from and where it went. Exportable to PDF for a bank or an investor.

Not a prototype and not a design mock-up. This is the product as it runs today, with real documents, real money and legally valid signatures.
All figures on these screens belong to the founder's own company and are shown with consent; counterparty names are masked. The same interface is available inside Telegram as a Mini App and in a browser as an installable web application.

06
The effect for the country

The state moved the rules into digital form. We give business the tool to work inside them

Time given back

40 minutes → 2 minutes for an invoice. An ordinary VAT-registered company files 48 times a year and issues dozens of documents a month.

The country issues 3.5 million electronic invoices a month. Every half hour saved is working time returned to the economy rather than spent carrying figures between programs.

Fines that never happen

A wrong product code costs 1% of the sale value under Article 223 of the Tax Code. For a sole trader that doubles the annual tax bill.

The name behind a code is always taken from the state Tasnif catalogue and never composed by the model. For breaching the marking rules, 254 businesses were fined in 2022 — and 1,083 in 2025.

Uzbek as a first language

2,484 interface strings in each of two languages. Uzbek in Latin script in the interface and in Cyrillic inside legal documents, as Uzbek judicial and business practice requires.

Not a translation layered over a Russian product but an equal language everywhere: in the bot, in the app, in printed PDFs and in the voice.

Given away free, with no registration

IKPU code lookup

A public tool on the website: type a product name, get codes from the state catalogue. No sign-in and no payment

Demo mode

The whole path of creating and signing a document on safe data — before a person tells us anything about themselves

An accounting reference

A glossary and guides: how to issue an invoice, what an IKPU code is, VAT, waybills, a comparison of e-document operators

The country's law is encoded in the product

Article 223 of the Tax Code and the Tasnif codes. The minimum wage as a calendar, not a constant — it changes by decree. The rule that a full-time salary cannot fall below the minimum wage and cannot be topped up with bonuses. The requirements of Law ZRU-547 on personal data, with versioned consent.

An international player arrives here with somebody else's templates and rewrites them for years.

There are 86 organisations in the system today — an early audience, and we say so plainly. The effect described above is proven on individual businesses; carrying it to the scale of the country is the work of the year ahead.

Who built this

A platform on an enterprise scale, built by a small team with AI

A volume of work that normally takes several dozen engineers and a couple of years was built in six months, with artificial intelligence as the primary development tool. That is not a curiosity but a working method: we apply to ourselves exactly what we sell to the client.

2,280commits since 12 February 2026
1,198merged pull requests — work goes through review
155days with commits out of 193 calendar days — 80%
1,321test files out of 3,188 — 41% of the codebase
engineering discipline
  • Circuit breakers on nine external systems — a provider's failure does not take the product down with it
  • Idempotent signing with verification of the actual state after a dropped connection
  • 117 kill switches — any feature can be stopped in a second with no release
  • 256 database migrations, each reversible and verified in the pipeline
verifiability
  • Over 18,000 automated tests in Python and 3,500 in TypeScript
  • Every night the entire repository history is re-examined for an accidentally committed secret, by two independent scanners
  • A 4,000-line product overview in which every figure is reconciled against the code and production automatically
  • Automatic deployment rollback — a failed release restores the previous state by itself

The risk we name ourselves

A key dependency on one person. We acknowledge it and do not hide it.

It is removed by hiring; the documentation, the tests and the overview are built so that a handover is possible rather than so that the knowledge lives in someone's head. Growing the team is the first line of spending.

09
Act I

The country has already gone digital. Business was left carrying it by hand

The state moved the rules of the game into electronic form — documents, cash registers, HR, payments. That was right and it is already done. What was not done is the other half: nobody gave business the tool to play by those rules.

One figure explains everything: the number of tax payments per year fell from 58 to 9 — while the time a business spends on them barely changed. Digitisation removed the queues and the payment slips. It did not remove the work.

Four spreads on what a working day looks like today — and what it costs
10
Context · the country

Uzbekistan is one of the fastest-digitising economies in the region

815kcompanies and entrepreneurs are required to run electronic documents
3.5melectronic invoices are issued every month
33.1minternet users — 89% of the population
×22growth in e-commerce over five years

What the state already requires to be done digitally

The invoice

Electronic only — since 2020. A signed file that the tax authority verifies before it becomes legally valid

The transport waybill

Electronic for every business entity since July 2024. From 2025 it merges with the invoice into a single document

The fiscal cash register

The receipt reaches the tax authority at the moment of sale

The labour register

Every employee is registered in a single national register

Digital product marking

Eight product groups. Since September 2025 an invoice without a marking code cannot be issued at all

Statistical reporting

Electronic only, and only with a digital signature

Cashless payments

A sale without electronic payment or a QR code — a fine of 5 million UZS

Open banking

To be implemented by 1 September 2026 under a presidential decree

Eight mandatory digital regimes. And not one tool that brings them together. The rules of the game went digital — business still plays them by hand.

And a mistake now costs a percentage of revenue. Breaching the marking rules costs up to 2% of the quarter's net revenue for a first offence and up to 20% for repeats. In 2022, 254 businesses were fined. In 2025 — 1,083.

On top of that: the tax authority scores companies automatically against 59 risk criteria, and from 2026 it assigns a risk level to every invoice in real time and checks marking compliance remotely. A mistake has stopped being the bookkeeper's internal affair — it is now visible to the state before it is visible to the owner.

12
The problem · what it really costs

It is not about the lost hours. It is about three holes through which money leaves

Deals that never close

The contract is signed, the goods shipped, the act completed — and no payment arrives. Nobody notices, because nobody reconciles contracts against the bank statement.

Overdue receivables in the country have grown 11.9-fold in four years — while receivables themselves grew 2.5-fold. Arrears are growing four times faster than the debt.

And recovering it through the courts costs 20.5% of the claim and 225 days.

An owner who cannot see

The founder looks at the business once a quarter, through a report in a language they were never required to understand. By the time the dividends come in lower than expected, it is too late to investigate.

Panic at the moment of risk

A demand arrives from the tax office. The owner has no idea how serious it is, who to turn to, or what it ought to cost. The first firm they call can name any number it likes.

All three holes open in the same place: where the money, the documents and the goods sit in different programs — and nobody looks at them at the same time.
This is exactly the work an attentive bookkeeper does by hand today — and which is physically impossible to do attentively every day, for years.

The moment · why now

Almost everyone has artificial intelligence. Almost nobody has working agents

The world has already agreed that the future belongs to agents — and almost nobody has managed to launch one. Between "we are trying AI" and "AI does the work" lies a chasm, and the whole industry has fallen into it.

88%

of organisations already use AI in at least one function

11%

have an AI agent in real production use, not in a pilot

10%

is the ceiling on agent scaling — no business function goes higher

Why it fails for them and works for us

A general-purpose assistant does not know your industry, your law or your documents — so it advises rather than acts. We built an agent that lives inside the state infrastructure of one country: it knows what an invoice looks like, what a classifier code is, and what a missed reply to the tax office costs. Hence the difference between "a pilot" and "137,617 documents".

The solution · three levels of value

We are not an eleventh tool to add to ten. We are the layer in which they finally work together

In places we integrate with what the client already uses. In others we replace it with a module of our own. But always so that the business has one way in and one picture of reality.

level 1

A tool

An invoice in two minutes instead of forty. By voice, from a phone, digitally signed — with no computer and no bookkeeper at your side.

level 2

A loop

A document is part of a deal. The system sees: contract signed → no payment → power of attorney issued → invoice not raised — and says whose move it is.

level 3

An orchestrator

A storefront order becomes a contract and an invoice by itself. A payment closes the deal by itself. A till receipt posts itself to the books. A tax letter arrives in the messenger by itself.

And above all of it — the voice. The owner talks; the business works.
The three levels are not price plans and not rollout stages. They are the depth a client goes to on their own, as trust grows.

The main bet · the AI orchestrator

The owner talks.
The business works.

Not "voice input" and not "commands to an assistant". A manager — an AI that knows this company in full: its products and prices, its counterparties and how reliably they pay, its stock, its debts, its deadlines. You speak to it the way you would speak to a capable managing director.

"What's happening with Artel?"
"How much tax do we owe before the end of the month?"
"Invoice them for the same laptops as last time, but at the new price"
"Who hasn't paid for over a month — write to all of them"

And it does it — it does not find a menu section, it performs the operation in the system.

Why this is possible here specifically

  • The voice can do exactly what the app can. Not a cut-down branch of code — the same operations with the same checks on amounts, VAT and codes
  • Every new feature becomes a voice feature immediately. We never build a feature twice
  • It sees the whole business at once. The question "can we ship on credit?" needs the deal history, payment discipline, stock levels, receivables and the account balance. In any other system that is four programs and half a day of a bookkeeper's time
phonebrowsercomputervoice messages in the bot
Speech and the content of the conversation are processed in zero-retention mode — and we do not assume that, we verify it on a schedule.

What actually happened here

Seven events in a working day. Four the system closed completely, three it brought to the owner — and each of the three is settled with one tap, not a trip into another program.

The owner does not confirm a hundred operations a day. They look at the feed of what was done and take a handful of real decisions — the kind that made them the owner.

Where we are heading: 99 operations out of 100 the agent, one the owner

This is a goal we are moving towards deliberately, not a property of today. Giving the agent the right to act without asking requires the owner's explicit permission, limits by amount and counterparty, one-tap revocation and a feed of what was done — that work is under way.
24
The rule that is never broken

The AI proposes — a human confirms. And that lives in the code, not in a promise

Every irreversible operation — signing, sending, accepting a document, making a payment — passes through a confirmation card. The AI prepares, calculates, fills in and explains, but does not sign on its own.

The confirmation phrase is composed by the server

When the orchestrator says "signing invoice No. 145 for 18 million for Artel", those words were assembled by code out of the operation about to execute. The model cannot say one thing and do another.

Identity is not the voice

Voiceprints are neither collected nor compared. A person is identified exactly as in the app — by a session signature. A recorded voice grants access to nothing.

The product name comes from the state catalogue

The classifier code and its official name are taken from the register and never composed by the model: a wrong code is a fine.

Anomalies are found by rules, not by AI

The odd-transaction detector runs on strict logic: falsely accusing a bookkeeper costs more than missing a finding.

Forty minutes on the portal become two minutes by voice

Agent on a PCthe key never leaves your computer, the job arrives from your phone

Signing always begins with a human action. If the connection drops, the system verifies the document's actual state rather than blindly signing a second time.

Official mass-mailing of commercial proposals. Up to 20,000 recipients in one action: each receives their own signed document in their working account. With document operators this is sent one at a time, by hand.

Module · AI Lawyer

It will draft your articles of association — and win back your money

A lawyer on staff is expensive, a lawyer on call arrives late. This one lives inside the system

What it does

Debtsformal claim, debt letter, rescheduling agreement
Courtstatement of claim, application for a court order, response to a claim
Contractssupply, lease, services, works, promissory note, power of attorney
The companyarticles of association, sole-member resolution, minutes, admitting a new founder, changing shares

The scenario it was built for

  • The system sees: contract signed, goods shipped — no payment
  • It notifies the owner
  • The lawyer pulls the facts out of your own database: the contract number and date, its payment clauses, the amount, how far overdue it is
  • It drafts a claim citing the specific clauses, with the interest calculated
  • Still unpaid — the same loop prepares a lawsuit with the claim amount already computed

Why it can be trusted

Statute citations are verified. If the model cites an article that does not exist, the citation simply does not pass.

Money is calculated by code, not by a language model. Interest, penalties and deadlines come from a deterministic calculator.

Articles of association are not composed freely. The cost of an error in a founding document is out of all proportion to the convenience, so there is a strict process rather than AI creativity.

The corpus of statutes is topped up from official sources; the official Uzbek text is authoritative. Citations are clickable directly inside the message.

Modules · money and the state

"Has the money arrived?" stops being a question

The bank, the till and the tax office come to you themselves — into the messenger you already live in

iBank — every bank in one window

The bank is not "one more integration" but the source of truth about money. Without it neither deals nor Business Pulse can work.

  • A credit arrives as a push — with the amount, the sender and the contract it belongs to. Instead of phoning the bookkeeper every half hour
  • A direct bank connection plus statement import from any format — including PDF and 1C
  • The payment order is sent from here too, signed with your digital signature — no trip into the bank client
  • The payment reference code stops being a mystery: the system fills it in — a beginner pays for that mistake out of their own pocket
  • A single money ledger — one place where every section asks "has this been paid?"
  • Reconciliation in both directions: money without documents, documents without money
  • Cash flow and a finished Excel register allocated across business units
59,354bank transactions already parsed

The tax office

Today a business has to log into the portal with a key and check whether a notice has arrived. Miss it, and you miss the deadline to reply.

  • The system checks the mailbox for you — freshness of about an hour instead of a day
  • The letter arrives in Telegram, with an explanation: what they want, by when, and what happens if you do not reply
  • A deadline reminder — before the due date, not after
  • Fiscal cash register: receipts into the books, sales and refunds kept apart, an evening till summary
  • Reconciliation: what went through the till against what was issued as documents

Legally correct opening. Until you explicitly confirm, the letter is shown as a headline only: a read receipt starts legal deadlines running, and the system has no right to set it by accident.

For the owner of three companies this changes the working regime: three organisations, one notification feed, one tap to switch, a reaction on the same day.

Modules · sales

Everywhere else an order ends in a basket. Here it ends in a closed deal with the bookkeeping done

UmagShop

A shared catalogue and a shop on your own subdomain. An order becomes an ordinary deal: contract → payment → invoice → acceptance → closure.

The AI assistant picks products out of the catalogue rather than naming them — an invented price has physically nowhere to land.

QR-Hisob

A printed sheet with a QR code on the counter. A business buyer scans it, enters their tax number and places the order — with no registration and no app.

The seller receives a card: one tap and the contract is signed, one more and the invoice is issued.

Deal Link

The seller sends a link into a messenger, the buyer fills it in and receives a contract and an invoice. Payment deadline, statuses, SMS, automatic payment matching.

The page was written for a cold buyer arriving from a social network's in-app browser.

Nasiya — instalments

Accounting for instalment sales for the seller who finances them personally. Schedule, late fees, a portfolio by days past due, seller shifts.

We are not a lender: the money and the risk stay with the seller; we provide the bookkeeping and the discipline.

The decision everything is built around

A product is not a listing. Purchase prices live apart from shop prices. A "publish everything" button exists neither in the interface nor in the API.

A business that suspects its purchase prices might leak will not put a single product on a storefront. So the guarantee is fixed in the code and in the tests: a dedicated test walks every public address and fails if even one private field leaks out. In the interface it is drawn as two columns — "In the system · only you see this" ↔ "In the shop · buyers see this" — with a caption on the divider: "nothing crosses on its own".

Honestly about the state of things: the storefront infrastructure works and the marketplace is filling up. There is no shortage of supply — 36 businesses already hold products in the system.

New modules · the way in and the way out of the ecosystem

We took the two edges accounting systems never reach

One before the business exists. The other where it trades on somebody else's floor

Business from scratch

launching

Almost all automation in the country addresses people who already have a business. Someone who has just decided to start is left alone with "where do I even begin?" — and goes off to pay an intermediary to fill in forms.

  • The intermediary charges for knowing the form, not for the work. That is exactly the kind of knowledge a system holds better than a person
  • The articles are not a downloaded template but text written for your structure: number of founders, shares, exit procedure, the director's powers
  • A mistake at the start costs months. The wrong activity code, the wrong tax regime, a missing clause — it all surfaces six months later
  • Day one does not end with registration. You need an account, e-documents, a signature key, a first contract — and all of that is already here

Where it grows. An agreement with the Ministry of Justice platform for API access, so that the application is filed without leaving the conversation.

iSeller

launching

An entrepreneur rarely sells in one place: their own shop, our storefront and listings on the marketplaces alongside. iSeller used to be a separate product — now it is part of the ecosystem.

  • Everyone calculates the commission; almost nobody calculates the economics. Sellers learn their real margin after the fact, once the platform has taken its cut and logistics cost more than planned
  • One catalogue across every channel. A product is entered once and then lives in the warehouse, on the storefront and in the marketplace listings, on shared stock
  • Sales come back into the books. An order from a marketplace is revenue like any other: it enters the money ledger, the reports and Business Pulse
  • And your own storefront alongside, where the same goods sell wholesale with a contract and an invoice

Why this is part of the ecosystem rather than a separate product. A marketplace seller is not a different person but the same entrepreneur in one more role: the same goods, the same money, the same tax office.

Together they widen the market in both directions: downwards, to people who do not have a business yet, and sideways, to those trading on other people's platforms.
Both modules have pages of their own on ihisobchi.uz. Neither needs a new core: they rest on the same documents, the same money ledger and the same AI agent.

Act IV · why this cannot be repeated

Any single feature can be copied. Copying the combination means building it all again

To repeat this you would have to raise the state document system, the digital signature, the bank, the tax office, the warehouse, the law and the artificial intelligence of one country at the same time — and hold them together for years. That is not a feature. That is a distance.

The moat, security, horizons and economics

Global context · the same category

Everyone has noticed the category. Nobody has walked into the state infrastructure

Over two years a whole wave of companies has risen worldwide building exactly this: AI that does the financial and operational work rather than helping someone do it. They are valued in billions. And all of them share one boundary.

WhoWhat they doWhat they stand on

hundreds of millions each		Bookkeeping that closes a period in daysNetSuite, QuickBooks, Xero

Not one of them is built into their country's tax authority, document system and digital signature. All of them are a layer over an accounting package. To them the state is an outside world the bookkeeper visits in person.

And that is exactly where we stand

  • For us the state infrastructure is not an integration but the foundation. 137,617 documents, 119,539 incoming ones and 59,354 bank transactions have already passed through it
  • Vertical agents are the fastest-growing segment of the AI market and grow markedly faster than the market as a whole
  • The state is officially becoming an agent's counterparty: analysts estimate that by 2028 at least 80% of governments will deploy AI agents for routine decisions
  • A product like this cannot be built globally. The electronic invoice, the signature and the tax authority are specific to each country. An international player arrives with somebody else's templates and rewrites them for years; only someone living inside this law can build the whole of it
We are not catching up with the global wave. We stand at its point — on the side it has not yet reached.
Valuations and rounds are from companies' official announcements and the business press, 2025–2026. The claim "nobody is built into the state infrastructure" is the result of a deliberate search: absence cannot be proven strictly, so we put it precisely — no player in the category valued above a billion operates inside its own country's state systems.

41
Trust · security

Businesses trust us with passwords, signature keys and commercial secrets. One incident is enough for nobody to trust us again

Encrypted before it reaches disk

Not "a database behind a password" — the values themselves are stored encrypted. Even complete access to the database yields no client passwords.

Data does not stay in the AI

Zero-retention mode — and we do not assume it, we verify it on a schedule, automatically.

The signing key in an envelope

In "24/7 server" mode the key is sealed so that ordinary production physically cannot read it. Most clients do not need this at all: their key never leaves their computer.

Killed in a second

Every risky feature sits behind a switch of its own that works without shipping a new version.

  • Not one password in the code — not a gentlemen's agreement but an automatic check: a commit containing a secret does not go through
  • Each client sees only their own data — the isolation is covered by tests
  • Employee data sits behind a separate lock: consent to bookkeeping is not consent to people's personal data
  • Other people's files are parsed in a sandbox with no access to the network or the database
  • File links are single-use — a forwarded link is useless
  • Versioned consent — the system remembers which revision of the policy you accepted, and when

And what we say ourselves

A legal review by an outside specialist in Uzbek law is a mandatory step before a wide public launch, and it is not finished. We keep three questions under watch and do not consider them closed: the scope of what is sent to the AI is described more narrowly in the policy than in fact, formal retention periods are not documented everywhere, and a formal data-protection officer has to be appointed.

We would rather show this list than declare a readiness that does not yet exist.

Every night, automatically: a check of zero-retention mode at the AI providers, a secret scan of the code, dependency updates, and verification of data isolation.

Economics

Nine revenue streams — and not one percentage of a client's deal

The first thing to say about our economics is what is absent from it

We take no commission on a client's turnover. Not on a deal, not on a payment, not on an order. The money goes straight from the buyer's account to the seller's — we neither hold it, nor route it, nor delay it. We work with the documents about money, not with the money.

Which means we have no conflict of interest: our revenue does not rise because a client sold at a higher price.

Subscription — the foundation

250kLight — sole traders and micro-business
490kPro — small business with a bookkeeper
990kMax — active trading, several companies

UZS per month. The plans are separated not by a number of buttons but by access to the heavy things: document volume, number of organisations, depth of AI use, external systems, signing modes.

The streams compound rather than compete. A client arrives for documents, then puts goods in the warehouse, then promotes them on the storefront. Each step is a distinct piece of value and a distinct payment, and all of them run on the same data.

The commercial loop is the youngest part of the product: the plans are defined, the payment loop is being built, access is granted by invitation. That is a deliberate sequence — first turn what works into regular use, then charge for it.

Values · what does not change

Five rules that hold on every horizon

They are the reason a business can entrust its money and its documents to the system at all.

The AI proposes — a human confirms

Autonomy is only ever widened through the owner's explicit consent, revocable and bounded by amount and duration. Never through "we decided it was more convenient".

The truth of the numbers

Bookkeeping has no right to be wrong about an amount, VAT, a date or a code. Anomalies are found by rules, not by a language model. One wrong figure costs more than ten new features.

Nothing crosses on its own

Purchase prices do not leak onto a storefront, employee data does not open up along with the bookkeeping, a tax letter is not marked as read without you.

Everything can be killed in a second

Every feature sits behind a switch of its own that works without shipping a new version. A provider's failure does not take the system down with it.

Uzbek is a first language, not a translation

Both languages carry equal weight everywhere: in the interface, in documents, in printed PDFs, in voice.

We are not building an accounting program. We are building an environment in which business in Uzbekistan runs itself.
46
In summary

The state moved the rules into digital form. We gave business the tool to work inside them

Goods sold → documents filed themselves → money arrived and allocated itself → the deal closed itself. The owner is left to watch, to check and to decide — which is what they opened the business for.

What it gives the country

Forty minutes of work become two, and the difference goes back to the entrepreneur. The error in a product code that costs one per cent of turnover stops happening. Uzbek is the product's first language, not a translation.

What is built

17 modules, 18 surfaces, 24 types of state document, 67 operations available to the AI. Running in production with legally valid document flow.

What does not change

Not one action without the owner's confirmation. Not one figure we cannot produce a document for. Not one percentage of a client's deal.
